### Hey, Professor. I still have time and energy and interest in reading!

**On logistic regression, one example of the *generalized linear model*.**

- [Chapter 12 of *Why Statistics*](https://catterson.github.io/ystats/chapters/12R_LogisticRegression.html)*.* The basics of how to adapt the linear model to predict a binary variable.

- [Generalized Linear Models](https://m-clark.github.io/book-of-models/generalized_linear_models.html). I like this researcher’s approach to linear models, and while this textbook chapter is a little more spare than some of the other chapters, it presents a nice overview of why and how we use generalized linear models.

- [A stats blog](https://www.datascienceblog.net/post/machine-learning/interpreting_generalized_linear_models/) works through the output of a generalized linear model in R; focuses on a poisson distribution, but many of the principles are the same (and good to see a different example of a similar concept.)
